method.resolution_rule: The audit derives current behavior from schemas, governed policies, validators, compilers and release gates before comparing documentation. It records documentation drift but does not itself replace normative authority.

findings.title: Canonical root omits upstream Engineering technical authority

evidence.observation: The root topology begins from Ground Truth through Core1/Core2 and says Core1 determines semantic authority, but it does not model the now-executable upstream Engineering authorization chain.

The newer normative boundary states that Engineering is upstream technical authority and that Blueprint may consume it only through exact digest-bound identities, generic validation and deterministic closure.
The Workbench validates the canonical Engineering registry, resolves only exact gate or linked-bucket identities, evaluates generic depth and computes prerequisite closure before authorization.
Engineering source identity is explicitly canonical mathematical identity for Engineering-derived Domain assets, with teaching scope represented separately as membership metadata.

findings.current_doctrine: Engineering is upstream technical mathematical authority. Core1 retains a semantic reconstruction authority role only inside already-authorized mathematical scope; Core2 retains assessment/source-question authority within that same layered system.
findings.c2_action: Rewrite the canonical authority topology to place non-authoritative discovery, exact Engineering selection/authorization, validation, closure and custody upstream of Domain projection and Core products, while preserving the narrower Core1/Core2 authority distinction.

findings.title: Dual-track EASY research rule conflicts with current governed policy

evidence.observation: Its SDU difficulty table says EASY has no pedagogy-enrichment web research, which reads as a prohibition.
The current generation-control boundary states that EASY research is optional, not prohibited, and must be fully bound when used.
The current pedagogy contract repeats that EASY web research is optional and explicitly separates research permission from research obligation.
The generation-spec validator treats OPTIONAL research as legal only when research refs and the brief ref are present or absent together.
The test suite explicitly proves that EASY permits optional bound pedagogy research and rejects a half-bound EASY research state.

findings.current_doctrine: Pedagogy-research discovery is permitted at every difficulty. EASY has no minimum research obligation, but optional promoted research is legal only when its brief and evidence binding are complete; MEDIUM and HARD retain targeted/deep obligations.
findings.c2_action: Remove the stale EASY research prohibition from the dual-track doctrine and use the current permission-versus-obligation rule consistently, while separately exposing the compiler materialization gap recorded by C0-F007.

findings.title: Canonical publication topology lags the governed semantic bundle path

evidence.observation: The root presents LearnerPageBlueprint followed by deterministic typesetting as the canonical publication path and does not describe the current release-bound semantic publication bundle.

The current publication contract binds release status, generation spec, governed examples, pedagogy research, Engineering visibility, concept components and the problem component into one semantic learner publication bundle.

The governed publication runner requires a passing release gate, compiles Engineering visibility, compiles and validates the semantic bundle, renders it and enforces LEARNER_PUBLICATION_BUNDLE_ONLY as semantic source.
Current product governance requires the validated embedded Engineering visibility object and preserves semantic_source = LEARNER_PUBLICATION_BUNDLE_ONLY.

findings.current_doctrine: LearnerPageBlueprint remains a repository contract, but the current governed bound-release publication path is release gate to semantic learner publication bundle to validated rendering, with research and Engineering-visibility custody bound before the PDF is accepted.
findings.c2_action: Distinguish any retained internal LearnerPageBlueprint role from the actual release/publication boundary and make the semantic publication bundle the canonical governed publication input in the consolidated root.

findings.title: Current non-authoritative Engineering discovery is absent from the canonical root

evidence.observation: Discovery is explicitly non-authoritative, may rank approximate candidates and requires a separate exact digest-bound selection before Engineering authority.
The receipt schema locks discovery to candidate-only authority, no automatic selection and no implied publication authorization.
The compiler ranks candidate identities and promotes only an explicit exact selection into the existing standard Engineering request path.

findings.current_doctrine: Human-language search, aliases and approximate matching may improve discoverability but never authorize mathematics. Authority begins only after explicit exact identity selection enters the unchanged exact Engineering resolver.
findings.c2_action: Add discovery as a non-authoritative pre-authority layer in the canonical root and preserve a visually explicit boundary between candidate ranking and exact technical authorization.

findings.title: Claim-level pedagogy research promotion is missing from the canonical root

evidence.observation: Current research promotion is decision-and-claim based, with SUPPORTS/CONTRADICTS evidence stance, confidence and explicit contradiction resolution.
The current manifest schema represents research sources, decisions, promoted claims, evidence links and release class rather than treating a URL list as promotion.
The validator enforces claim coverage, supporting evidence, contradiction handling, confidence and production-vs-test evidence rules.

findings.current_doctrine: Research discovery is permissive, while promotion into generation is claim-specific, evidence-custodied and fail-closed. Pedagogy evidence can change teaching design but cannot create mathematical or curriculum authority.
findings.c2_action: Replace dossier-only shorthand in the root with the current promotion boundary at an architectural level, while leaving field-level research contract detail in the subordinate specification.

findings.title: Derived Engineering visibility boundary is absent from the canonical root

evidence.observation: A released product may expose Engineering information only through a derived manifest that cannot modify technical readiness, scope or publication authorization.
The visibility contract distinguishes a derived view of bound Engineering authority and locks publication authorization to NOT_IMPLIED.
The compiler revalidates exact current Engineering custody before deriving learner/author visibility, rather than using the view as an authorization input.

findings.current_doctrine: Engineering visibility is a digest-bound explainability projection of already-authorized Engineering state. It may appear in publication, but it is never a technical or publication authorization path.
findings.c2_action: Add derived visibility between released product authority and semantic publication, and explicitly label it non-authoritative with publication authorization not implied.

findings.title: Canonical compiler does not materialize optional EASY research bindings

evidence.observation: The current policy says optional EASY research may be promoted when its brief and evidence references are fully bound.
The generation-spec validator supports EASY optional research and fails only when refs and brief are half-bound.
Validator tests prove a manually bound EASY row is legal and a half-bound row is illegal.

The canonical _bind_research implementation selects only non-EASY rows and writes decision/reference bindings only to those rows, so an EASY decision supplied in a manifest is not materialized into the compiled EASY bucket.
Generation research-binding validation iterates non-EASY buckets for promoted source retention, while an all-EASY spec merely validates the manifest and returns.

findings.current_doctrine: Optional EASY research is the current governed policy and is valid at the generation-spec validation boundary, but the canonical SDU/LAU compiler path does not yet materialize that optional binding automatically; this capability must not be described as fully compiler-executable until repaired and falsified.
findings.c2_action: Classify optional EASY research materialization as CURRENT + DOCUMENTED ONLY in the consolidated executable-reference table and schedule a separate governed compiler migration with a falsifier before upgrading it to CURRENT + EXECUTABLE.

confirmed_current_doctrine.statement: Execution order may vary, but authority order remains exact and fail-closed; approximate discovery cannot replace exact subject authorization.
Topic-specific mathematical truth belongs to governed Engineering data, while generic Blueprint code owns orchestration, closure, custody and downstream composition.
Core1 semantic reconstruction and Core2 assessment/source-question roles remain distinct downstream responsibilities, but neither may bypass upstream Engineering technical authority.
Engineering source identity is stored canonically once; teaching scope, direct/prerequisite role and local capability/question use are separate membership metadata.
SDU controls Core1A/Core1B depth from intrinsic Engineering-backed difficulty and never learner percentage; LAU controls Core2A/Core2B learner fit from governed evidence or explicit owner waiver.

The generation-spec validation contract implements the permission-versus-obligation rule: EASY research may be absent or fully bound, while MEDIUM/HARD require governed research; compiler materialization for optional EASY remains separately classified by C0-F007.

Product release revalidates current custody before publication, and governed publication consumes a semantic learner publication bundle rather than inventing missing mathematical or pedagogical semantics in the renderer.
Engineering visibility is derived explainability only: it is bound to exact current Engineering custody and explicitly cannot imply publication authorization.

notes: The C1 component decomposition is consistent with the independently derived executable architecture at responsibility level; no C1 component needs removal before C2.
C2 must reconcile the layered meaning of Core1 semantic authority with upstream Engineering technical authority rather than treating the C1 catalog as a replacement authority model.

The C1 CALIBRATION component is structurally real, but C0-F007 means one optional EASY research materialization path is documented/validator-supported rather than fully implemented by the canonical compiler.

The C1 inventory_snapshot base_head_sha predates the audited repository snapshot; this is harmless for a non-authoritative candidate but demonstrates why C3 generated references should use explicit immutable source-snapshot custody rather than a moving-current-tree claim.

required_remediations: Insert the exact Engineering technical-authority chain upstream of Core/domain/product authority in the consolidated root.
Preserve Core1 semantic and Core2 assessment roles as layered downstream authority, not as a replacement for Engineering technical authority.

Correct the stale EASY research prohibition to optional-but-governed research, while marking canonical compiler materialization for optional EASY research as documented-only until a separate executable migration closes C0-F007.
Make the semantic learner publication bundle the canonical bound publication input while documenting any retained LearnerPageBlueprint role accurately.
Add non-authoritative Engineering discovery, claim-level pedagogy promotion and derived Engineering visibility to the consolidated architecture boundary.
Keep design/audit/catalog artifacts non-authoritative and do not make production runtime consume design files.
